name: Berom
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Bouquiaux, Luc. 1970. La langue birom (Nigeria septentrional): phonologie, morphologie, syntaxe. Paris: Les Belles Lettres.
earlier_scan.note: Full phonology exists but not online; Wikipedia (read) describes 3 level + glide TONES for Berom, no stress statement

sources.citation: Ukaegbu, Nkechi M., Gideon S. Omachonu & Benita C. Odii. 2017. An autosegmental analysis of Berom tones and tonal processes. JOLAN: Journal of the Linguistic Association of Nigeria 20(1): 233-242.
sources.note: Riyom dialect. Three register tones H/M/L plus rising and falling contour tones, lexically and grammatically contrastive; TBUs are vowels and syllabic nasals; tone copying and tonal replacement. 'Stress' appears only in a generic remark that autosegmental theory cannot handle stress; nothing said about Berom stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. Research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 3-44.
sources.note: Section 2.3: 'The principal publications on Berom are Bouquiaux (1970, 2001)'; Bouquiaux describes the Du dialect (Central Berom); Kuhn & Dusu 1985 is the official orthography; Blench, Pwol, Dusu & Kuhn ined. = Berom dictionary. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed., entry 45 Berom.
sources.note: Lists sources only: Grammar Wolff (1963), Bouquiaux (1970) [Du]; Dictionaries Bouquiaux (2001), Blench et al (2016); Orthography Kuhn & Dusu (1985). No phonology reference beyond these.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. Plural verb morphology in Eastern Berom. Draft ms., Mallam Dendo, Cambridge, 2 January 2006. 20 pp.
sources.note: Section 2 'Berom phonology' (pp. 3-4): 24 consonants, 7 vowels, 'Berom has three level tones and four glide tones (Bouquiaux 1970)'; vowel length treated as sequences each bearing its own toneme. Nothing on stress/accent ('accent' occurs only as the orthographic acute mark for plurality).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Nincut language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft ms., Cambridge, 3 January 2006. 25 pp.
sources.note: Section 3.3 (p. 3): 'Nincut has three level tones and a rising and falling tone.' No mention of stress. (Nincut is a separate Beromic lect, formerly counted as a Berom dialect.)

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Tahoss dialect of the Berom language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft ms., Cambridge, 3 January 2006. 25 pp.
sources.note: Section 3.3 Tones (p. 4): 'Like other Berom lects, Tahos has three level tones' (H, M, L); apparent rising/falling tones are sequences of two like vowels. No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Bouquiaux, Luc. 1962. Textes birom (Nigeria septentrional). Africana Linguistica 1: 11-29. doi:10.3406/aflin.1962.855
sources.note: Transcription notes on p. 11 (Du dialect): 'Il y a en birom trois tons fondamentaux uniformes, dont la hauteur ne varie pas; ce sont les tons haut, moyen et bas. L'intervalle entre ces tons reste constant... le birom possède également deux variétés de tons ascendants et deux variétés de tons descendants.' Nothing on accent/stress. Only p. 11 is exposed as HTML on Persée; the PDF is behind an altcha challenge.
